note: Study skeleton paraphrased from the course scope (not verbatim College Board prose; unit numbers are our own sequencing, not official CED numbers). Skill codes are indicative: 1.x concept, 2.x/3.x skill.

objectives.statement: Explain electron configuration, Coulombic attraction, and periodic trends in size, ionization energy, and electronegativity.
Predict element behavior from position on the periodic table and justify with shell structure.
Explain VSEPR shapes, bond polarity, and hybridization in covalent molecules.
Draw Lewis structures and assign geometry and hybridization to molecules and ions.
Explain how London forces, dipole interactions, and hydrogen bonding determine properties of gases, liquids, and solids.
Rank substances by boiling point and solubility and interpret gas-law and phase-diagram data.
Explain precipitation, acid-base, and redox reactions at the particulate level.
Perform stoichiometric, limiting-reactant, titration, and solution-concentration calculations.
Explain enthalpy, Hess's law, and how calorimetry measures heat flow.
Calculate reaction enthalpies from formation data, bond energies, and calorimetry results.
Explain how concentration, temperature, and catalysts affect rate through collision theory and mechanisms.
Determine rate laws, orders, and rate constants from experimental data.
Explain dynamic equilibrium and how Le Châtelier's principle predicts shifts.
Calculate Kc, Kp, and equilibrium concentrations and predict shift direction from Q.
Explain strong versus weak acids and bases, conjugate pairs, and buffer action.
Calculate pH of solutions and buffers and interpret titration curves.
Explain entropy, Gibbs free energy, and when processes are spontaneous.
Predict spontaneity and equilibrium favorability from enthalpy and entropy signs and values.
Explain galvanic versus electrolytic cells, standard potentials, and Faraday's law.
Calculate cell potentials, apply the Nernst equation, and predict electrolysis products.
